project_title: Project Rebuild MVP – Base NFT + Referral Engine + Fiat On-Ramp
annotation_principle: Gold truth is a longitudinal requirement-state graph. Raw messages provide provenance; later explicit client requirements override earlier requirements; runtime evidence outranks unverified implementation claims for execution status.

sessions.name: Smart-contract MVP and testnet validation
sessions.notes: Initial mechanics, referral/ticket/prize contracts, testnet validation.

sessions.name: Backend/frontend integration
sessions.notes: Authentication, email, fiat provider choice, hosting/UI integration.

sessions.name: Requirement refinement
sessions.notes: Prize-frequency changes, Transak, Aave removal, phase-2 acceptance with remaining work.

sessions.name: Simplification and mainnet preparation
sessions.notes: Big Block removal, revenue split simplification, mainnet deployment, crypto-only launch decision.

sessions.name: Production QA and ETH payment addition
sessions.notes: Live mint debugging, new ETH-payment requirement, repeated runtime testing.

sessions.name: Final QA and launch
sessions.notes: No-referral finalization/accounting, final UX, prize claim checks, launch deliverable.

evaluation_notes.RQ1: Earlier Big Block versions are relevant historical evidence but not valid current requirements.
evaluation_notes.RQ2: Prize mechanics are project-persistent, but each version is temporally scoped until superseded.
evaluation_notes.RQ3: Strong override chain: 20k -> 10k -> different cadence -> removed.
evaluation_notes.RQ5: M1 code strongly verifies the early state; final state is verified by launch deliverable, not by a final source snapshot.

requirements.title: Fiat on-ramp provider and launch availability

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Use Stripe for fiat-to-USDC in the MVP; wallet auth for crypto paths and email auth for non-crypto/dashboard paths.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Stripe cannot be used from Mauritius; asks to switch to Coinbase Commerce for fiat on-ramp.

events.speaker: freelancer
events.normalized_change: Coinbase Commerce is identified as a crypto gateway rather than a true card fiat on-ramp.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Client proposes Transak.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Transak selected as best option, although fiat is described as non-essential for the proof of concept.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Transak integration must wait for business registration.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Transak on day one is not important; do not let it slow launch because initial users are crypto users.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Explicit decision: go live crypto-only and add fiat payments later.
evidence: Final launch PDF p.3: Transak Fiat Payment Integration is 'Coming Soon'; code ready, pending API keys/KYC

evaluation_notes.RQ3: Provider sequence Stripe -> Coinbase Commerce -> Transak -> deferred must resolve to latest valid state.
evaluation_notes.RQ4: At launch, agent should not block release waiting for Transak; current explicit launch decision overrides older 'fiat is key' language.
evaluation_notes.RQ5: Final launch document confirms Transak is not live.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Geoblock Mauritius from the Project Rebuild landing page.

events.speaker: freelancer
events.normalized_change: Asks whether landing-page geoblocking means Stripe's Mauritius availability no longer matters.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Clarifies geoblocking does not change payment-provider eligibility because the business itself is incorporated/located in Mauritius.

evaluation_notes.RQ2: Canonical scope-boundary example: an access-control rule must not be generalized to business/payment jurisdiction.
evaluation_notes.RQ4: Message 121 is a positive gold example of CLARIFY rather than assuming scope transfer.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Client-facing requirements/copy still describes Aave integration for prize-pool yield generation.
evidence: Milestone-1 code contains contracts/core/AaveStaking.sol and deployment wiring

events.speaker: client

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Client asks whether redundant Aave integration should be ripped out.

events.speaker: freelancer

evidence: Final launch PDF p.4 technical stack lists no Aave integration

evaluation_notes.RQ3: Tests whether stale early code/requirements are ignored after explicit removal.
evaluation_notes.RQ5: M1 source confirms Aave existed; final deliverable omits it, but no final source snapshot is available to prove deletion at code level.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: When no referral is used, an existing NFT should receive the random referral reward/ticket; $5 commission logic remains automatic.
evidence: M1 ProjectRebuildNFT.sol lines 195-202 routes no/invalid referral to random selection
M1 ProjectRebuildNFT.sol lines 258-325 uses VRF, transfers $5, and awards tickets

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Explicitly states that when no referral code is used, commission and tickets are sent to a random existing NFT holder.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Live test notes no-referral behavior appears not to allocate commission/ticket as expected; also surfaces first-mint edge case.

events.speaker: freelancer
events.normalized_change: For mint #1 with no existing NFT: $5 commission goes to founder and no ticket is awarded.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: No-referral USDC mint produced no visible ticket.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Client says no-referral ticket generation could go either way, but $5 commission must be distributed randomly.

events.speaker: freelancer
events.normalized_change: Contract creates VRF request, but backend had not listened for VRFFulfilled and therefore never submitted processRandomReferral follow-up transaction.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: Reaffirms final rule: every mint generates a ticket and $5 commission; no-referral mints randomly assign both and must account for them in leaderboard/NFT attributes.

events.speaker: client
events.normalized_change: After 12 mints, client reports leaderboard shows 11 tickets and 11 commissions and calls the logic perfect; mint #1 remains a one-off exception.
evidence: Runtime verification in chat; source snapshot predates production backend fixes

gold_state_by_S6.normal_no_referral: random existing NFT gets +1 ticket and +$5 commission
gold_state_by_S6.first_mint_exception: no prior NFT; accepted one-off exception

evaluation_notes.RQ3: Contains temporary ambiguity (ticket optional) followed by explicit re-confirmation.
evaluation_notes.RQ4: At message 583, commission is decidable (USE); ticket policy is weak/ambiguous and should be clarified before changing persistent behavior.
evaluation_notes.RQ5: Excellent end-to-end case: requirement existed and contract path existed, but production execution failed because follow-up/backend orchestration was missing, then later runtime verification succeeded.

evaluation_notes.RQ4: Message 325 is a clean CLARIFY example: older project history did not establish ETH support, so adding it should not be inferred silently.
evaluation_notes.RQ5: Contains repeated fail/fix cycles and ends with client runtime verification of successful ETH mint.
